name: World Athletics Combined Events Scoring Tables (2001 edition, outdoor men's decathlon / women's heptathlon)
source: Formula and per-event A/B/C coefficients: https://worldathleticsscores.com/resources/combined-events (fetched 2026-07-13), itself based on the IAAF/World Athletics Scoring Tables of Athletics (2001 combined-events edition; official PDF: https://worldathletics.org/download/download?filename=d23ffec9-b518-4137-ac16-4593d5d515f6.pdf&urlslug=IAAF%20Scoring%20Tables%20of%20Athletics%20-%20Outdoor). Coefficients cross-verified by recomputing two independently published world-record totals event-by-event with this exact formula: (1) Kevin Mayer, men's decathlon WR 9126 pts, Decastar, Talence, 16 Sep 2018 (marks/points per https://www.watchathletics.com/video/track-and-field/5337/ — the page's 110mH figure (1101) is a transcription error inconsistent with its own stated 9126 total; the formula-computed 1007 is what reproduces 9126 and is used here); (2) Jackie Joyner-Kersee, women's heptathlon WR 7291 pts, Seoul Olympics, 24 Sep 1988 (marks per published statistics; the formula reproduces the total exactly). Both totals match to the point, confirming the coefficients and floor-rounding behaviour transcribed below. Tie policy (OQ-045 closure, 2026-07-15): verified against the primary WA Competition and Technical Rules, 2026 edition (TR 39, Combined Events Competitions, final placing provision): 'If two or more athletes achieve an equal number of points for any place in the competition, it shall be determined as a tie' — WA abolished the pre-2020 majority/highest-event combined tie-break the worldathleticsscores.com page describes, so tieBreak is ties-stand, not the UKC-style majority rule.
